first.text: You're awake! I thought you were Hushed. Or dead. Hushed is worse — dead people don't hum.
…Is that an ember? In your HAND? Does it hurt? Can I— no. Don't let me touch it.

choice.text: Where am I?
Who are you?
You said the fog leaves things behind?
Where was that humming thing again?
I found it. The humming pebble.
How are your lost things?
The beacon needs a Remnant. Could it be the pebble?
Here. Your pebble back. The beacon didn't need it.
The beacon's lit.
Mara's hung a green lantern by her door.
See you, Pell.

where.text: Shingle Point. Saltmarrow's up the boardwalk. Well — most of it. The north end's gone grey.
Don't go in the grey. You forget stuff. First little stuff, then you forget to come back.

who.text: Pell. I mend nets for Mara — she's the harbormaster. And I find things.
The fog spits stuff out on the tide. Buttons. A doll's arm. Once, a whole door. Nobody remembered whose.

offer.text: Lately it spits out things that are… warm. There's one by the big rocks, north-west. It hums.
I tried to grab it but my head went soft, like when you forget a word you just had.
You've got an ember, though. Maybe the fog can't get in your head. Will you fetch it?

choice.text: I'll get it.
Not right now.

accepted.text: North-west, by the big rocks. Don't stand in the grey too long, even with that thing.

still_looking.text: North-west rocks. Follow the humming. You'll know it when your teeth start to itch.

pebble_return.text: You got it! And you still know your name? …You do know your name, right?
The pebble hums against your palm. For a moment you almost know the tune: a woman's voice, a cradle rocking in a boat.
That song… Mara used to hum it. Before. She can't remember the end anymore. Nobody can.
Can I keep it? I'll put it with my lost things. It'll be safe there.

choice.text: It's yours, Pell.
I should hold on to it. It might matter.

gave.text: Really? …Thanks. I'll keep it somewhere dry. I'll keep it forever.

kept.text: Oh. Yeah. Okay. It's probably important. Wakebearer stuff.
Just — don't lose it, all right? Somebody should remember that song.

collection.text: The pebble hums at night. I sleep better. Don't tell Mara, she'll say I've gone soft.

ask_pebble.text: Pell's hand goes to their pocket and stays there.
If it burns, nobody gets the song. Not even the wrong way I hum it. That's what the Keeper said, right? Gone gone.

choice.text: Yes. Gone for good. I'm sorry.
Keep it, Pell. I'll find another way.

ask_pebble_truth.text: …Mara can't finish it anyway. Nobody can. Maybe a song nobody can finish is the right thing to burn.
They put the pebble in your hand and close your fingers over it, hard, like it might try to get back out.
Don't tell me when you do it. I don't want to feel it go.

pebble_back.text: You didn't— it's still humming. It's still HUMMING.
I'm not crying. It's the smoke. From the beacon. Which is really far away.

lit.text: I saw it from the harbor! Gold! The fog's gone all the way back past the wall — I can see the lofts again!
Mara's got everyone mending. Funny — nobody can say what the first knot was. Like it's on the tip of your tongue, forever.
Mara's been setting out two cups at supper. Then she stares at the second one. Is that a grown-up thing?

lit_pebble.text: The fog's gone back past the harbor wall! You did it!
I had a pebble. I know I had one. I keep reaching in my pocket and there's just… pocket.
Mara was humming at the nets this morning. Then she stopped halfway and couldn't think what she'd been humming.
Weird. Everything's so quiet at night now.

ferry_lantern.text: I SAW! Green means the ferry! Green means passengers waiting! I've never seen it lit. Not once, not ever.
Mara says it used to come every fortnight, and there was a horn. She did it for me. HOOOOM. She's bad at it.
…You're going on it, aren't you. To Cindermoor.
Take me. I can mend nets. I can find things. I'm small, I don't take up a whole seat.

choice.text: When the ferry comes, you can come.
You belong here, Pell. Mara needs you.
Ask me again when you hear the horn.

ferry_promised.text: You mean it? You MEAN it. I'm packing. I've got a LOT of lost things to pack.
Don't tell Mara yet. I'll tell her. Later. Much later.

ferry_refused.text: …Yeah. Somebody has to find things here.
Fine. FINE. Bring me something back, then. Something lost. Something good.

ferry_undecided.text: That's a grown-up yes that means no. Or a grown-up no that means yes. I'll ask. I'll be LOUD.

dock.text: You're the one with the ember! Everybody says. I'm Pell. I find things.

dock_ask.text: It CAME. A real ferry, with a horn, and a lady with a SCALE. She weighs people. Not their bodies. Their— doings.
You're going on it. Take me. I can mend nets, I can find things, I'm small. I don't take up a whole seat.

choice.text: Yes. Come with me.
No, Pell. You stay.

dock_ask_again.text: HOOOOM. That was the horn. You said ask when I heard the horn. So I'm asking. LOUD.
Can I come? Can I? I'll be good. I'll be mostly good.

choice.text: Yes. Come with me.
No, Pell. You stay.

dock_yes.text: YES. Yes yes yes. I already packed. I packed when I heard the horn, just in case.
…Mara doesn't know. You tell her? You're better at words. I'm better at hiding.

dock_packed.text: Pell is sitting on a sailcloth bundle at the foot of the dock, kicking their heels.
Did you tell Mara? You didn't tell Mara. Oda says I can't cross without my kin's say. Mara's the nearest thing I've got to kin.

dock_pouch.text: …Yeah. I know. Somebody has to find things here.
Pell digs in a pocket and holds out a lumpy little pouch of sailcloth, a gull's feather stitched to the flap.
I made it out of the crate lining. It's for the lost thing. Bring me something lost. Something GOOD.
Don't come back with it empty.

dock_aboard.text: SHE SAID YES. Then she went inside and shut the door and I heard her blow her nose. Mara never blows her nose.
Oda says I'm on ropes. I'm going to be the BEST at ropes.

dock_let_down.text: It's fine. It's FINE. Somebody has to find things here.
Pell doesn't look at you. The bundle stays packed.

dock_stayed.text: Remember. Something lost. Something GOOD. Not a sock.

thornwold.text: Bram's got me sorting nails. Bent ones, straight ones, ones that were bent and got straightened. That last lot's the biggest.
The fog here spits out different things to ours. Pine-smell things. I found a cutter's tally stick by the sacks: somebody's count of something, and the last notch is only half cut.
Mara would say put it back where you found it. So I did. Then I took it again.

choice.text: Stay near the camp, Pell.
Keep looking. Tell me what you find.

thornwold_stay.text: I KNOW. Everybody says. Bram says it with nails.

thornwold_look.text: Course I will. You're the only one here who doesn't think finding things is just picking things up.
